sections.h2: What written notice must a Virginia landlord give before an eviction?
sections.html:
The notice depends on the reason, and a court will not enter an order of possession unless the landlord presents a proper termination notice and the court admits it into evidence. Rent problems, lease breaches, and the end of a month-to-month tenancy each follow different clocks.

SituationNotice periodCode section
Unpaid rent14 days after written notice to pay55.1-1245(F)
Breach that can be fixedLease ends no sooner than 30 days after receipt if not fixed in 21 days55.1-1245(A)
Breach that cannot be fixedNo sooner than 30 days after receipt55.1-1245(C)
Criminal or willful act threatening health or safetyImmediate termination and a possession case55.1-1245(C)
Week-to-week tenancy7 days before the next rent due date55.1-1253(A)
Month-to-month tenancy30 days before the next rent due date, unless the lease says otherwise55.1-1253(A)

sections.h2: How does the nonpayment notice work?
sections.html:
A landlord serves a written notice that the rent is unpaid and that the lease will end if it is not paid within 14 days. If the tenant pays in that window, the landlord cannot terminate on that notice.

The same 14-day route applies when a rent check bounces or an electronic payment is rejected for insufficient funds. In that case the notice must say the rent must be paid by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or completed electronic funds transfer.

A change takes effect on July 1, 2027. From that date, a landlord who owns more than four rental units in Virginia, or more than a 10 percent interest in more than four, must first send a notice stating the exact amount owed if the debt is no more than one month's rent plus contracted late charges. The notice must offer a payment plan over the lesser of six months or the time left on the lease, and the landlord has to offer that plan only once during the lease term.

  • Before July 1, 2027: 14-day written notice, then possession under 55.1-1251.
  • From July 1, 2027: larger landlords add the exact-amount notice and payment plan offer.
  • Late fees stop accruing on the covered debt while the tenant keeps up with the plan.

sections.h2: What happens when a tenant breaks other lease terms?
sections.html:
For a breach the tenant can correct, the landlord serves a notice that names the acts and omissions and says the lease ends on a date at least 30 days after receipt if the breach is not remedied within 21 days. If the tenant fixes it before the date, the lease does not end.

If a tenant repeats a like breach after fixing the first one, the landlord may serve a notice that refers to the prior breach and ends the lease no sooner than 30 days after receipt, with no new cure period.

Serious conduct is different. Illegal drug activity involving a controlled substance, or another criminal or willful act that threatens health or safety, counts as an immediate nonremediable violation, even if the tenant did not personally act, since the tenant is presumed to know of activity by an authorized occupant, guest, or invitee unless the tenant proves otherwise. The landlord does not need to wait for a criminal conviction, and the court sets an initial hearing within 15 calendar days of service. A later hearing or trial follows within 30 calendar days of service.

sections.h2: What does the court process look like after notice?
sections.html:
The landlord files a sworn statement and gets a summons for unlawful detainer from a magistrate, clerk, or judge of the general district court. For residential tenancy cases the first hearing should occur within 21 days of filing, and no later than 30 days if the court cannot hear it sooner.

The summons must be served at least 10 days before the return day. The landlord may ask for all rent due as of the hearing date and may amend the figure if more comes due before the case ends. Rent is not prorated to the hearing date if the lease makes rent due on the first for the whole month and the landlord asks for the full month.

  • File the sworn statement and get the summons.
  • Serve the tenant at least 10 days before the return date.
  • Attend the first hearing within 21 days of filing, or 30 at the latest.
  • Present the termination notice and the lease; photocopies are allowed with an affidavit.

A judge who grants possession can order the writ of eviction to issue immediately if the landlord asks. The summons also carries a notice that employers may not punish a tenant for missing work to appear in court.

sections.h2: How long do the tenant's appeal and the sheriff's writ take?
sections.html:
The tenant has 10 days to appeal a general district court judgment to the circuit court, and the sheriff may not evict before that 10-day period ends. A tenant who appeals must post a bond and pay the writ tax within the same 10 days, although an indigent defendant does not have to post an appeal bond.

Once a writ issues, the sheriff must serve notice of intent to execute at least 72 hours before the eviction, including the date and time. A writ must be issued within 180 days of the possession judgment and is returnable within 30 days. If it is not executed in 30 days, it is vacated as a matter of law.

No writ issues if, after the possession judgment, the landlord signs a new written rental agreement with the tenant. A landlord who waits past 180 days has to start over with a new case.

sections.h2: What about occupants who have no lease, or a former owner after foreclosure?
sections.html:
Virginia treats these cases differently. If an owner of a single-family home proves that no rental agreement ever existed, the occupant has no permission to be there, and the owner gave written notice to vacate at least 72 hours before filing, the court sets an emergency hearing within 14 days of filing, or 30 days at the outside.

If a former owner remains in a single-family home on the date of a foreclosure sale, that person becomes a tenant at sufferance. The new owner can end the tenancy with a written notice given at least three days before the effective date, then file for unlawful detainer. The former owner owes fair market rent from the sale date, plus damages, attorney fees, and court costs.

The squatters rights and adverse possession page on this site covers a separate legal question, so do not mix the two.

sections.h2: What does a landlord recover after the lease ends?
sections.html:
The landlord can seek possession and unpaid rent, plus actual damages, reasonable attorney fees, and service costs. Code 55.1-1251 does not allow a post-possession judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term, and the landlord must mitigate damages.

A court may enter a judgment for money and possession at the same time without crediting the security deposit. After the tenant leaves, the deposit is credited under the Virginia deposit rules.

A tenant who stays after the lease ends without consent can be sued for possession and actual damages. A lease may include a liquidated damage amount of up to 150 percent of the daily rent for each day the tenant remains, and the limit is the plain daily rent for public or HUD-regulated housing.

sections.h2: How does an eviction notice affect selling the house?
sections.html:
If you are the landlord and you want to sell, you must still end or honor the tenancy through the legal steps above. Sending a notice does not by itself clear the house, and the sheriff, not the landlord, carries out a writ.

  • List your notice dates and the case number, if one exists.
  • Say whether the tenant pays, and how much is behind.
  • Photograph the property and gather the lease, receipts, and any damage records.

We buy houses as-is, including rentals with a tenant in place or vacant houses that need work. Share the facts and we will tell you what we can offer. For legal questions, such as the validity of a particular notice, speak with a Virginia landlord-tenant attorney or a legal aid office.

faqs.q: How many days notice is required for unpaid rent in Virginia?
faqs.a: The landlord must give written notice and wait 14 days for payment before terminating the lease and seeking possession, under Code 55.1-1245(F).

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Virginia?
faqs.a: Either side must give written notice at least 30 days before the next rent due date, unless the rental agreement sets a different period, under Code 55.1-1253.

faqs.q: Can a Virginia landlord evict immediately for criminal activity?
faqs.a: Yes, in limited cases. A criminal or willful act that threatens health or safety, including illegal drug activity, allows immediate termination and a possession case, and the landlord does not need to wait for a conviction.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to appeal an eviction judgment?
faqs.a: The tenant has 10 days to appeal to the circuit court, and the sheriff cannot evict before that period ends under Code 8.01-129.

faqs.q: How long is a writ of eviction valid in Virginia?
faqs.a: It must be issued within 180 days of the possession judgment and executed within 30 days of issuance, or it is vacated under Code 8.01-471.

faqs.q: When do the new payment plan rules take effect?
faqs.a: The payment plan rule for landlords with more than four rental units takes effect July 1, 2027, according to the version of Code 55.1-1245 published for that date.
